title: cat is a byte identity
claim: cat reproduces its input byte-for-byte (cat < F equals F), and cat F F is exactly twice the bytes of F — cat is the identity carrier the switches ride on.
statements: cat < F equals F, byte for byte
cat F F is exactly twice the size

title: the encoding switch and the direction switch commute
claim: a per-character map (tr) and a reversal (rev) commute — tr then rev equals rev then tr — because a per-character map does not depend on position.
statements: tr|rev == rev|tr for several strings

title: every 7-bit margin state resolves to one of the 16 Fano constants in at most two steps
claim: the step "mark a XOR b for every marked pair" (one OR of three ANDs per point) reaches a fixed point in at most two steps for all 128 inputs; the fixed points are exactly the 16 XOR-closed masks (empty, 7 points, 7 lines, full); and, ordered as in core/src/verified/fano.ts (0 empty, 1..7 points, 8..14 lines, 15 full), the dual of index i is i XOR 15, i.e. perp(CONSTANTS[i]) == CONSTANTS[i XOR 15]. (Gemini's engine, checked against the author's verified fano.ts.)
statements: every state converges in <= 2 steps to a fixed mask that is a constant
exactly 16 fixed points
all sixteen table entries are constants (fixed points)
the dual law perp(CONSTANTS[i]) == CONSTANTS[i XOR 15] for all i

title: svg-switch toggles the payload, never the frame; twice is identity
claim: scripts/svg-switch --rev reverses only the content of <text>/<tspan>, leaves tags and attributes byte-identical, and applied twice returns the exact original. Frame vs payload = literal vs reading.
statements: the frame is untouched — the text tag with its attributes survives byte-for-byte
a non-text element is untouched
the payload did change — direction toggled
twice is the identity — byte-identical to the original

title: append extends the file; the complement of truncate
claim: `>>` appends — after `printf A > F; printf B >> F`, F is A+B and grew by exactly |B|. `>` replaces, `>>` keeps and extends. (F is not an input to the command — see ../pending.)
statements: the content is A followed by B
the file grew by exactly |B| = 3
strictly larger than before

title: an applet's name is the leaf of its install path
claim: `busybox --list` equals `busybox --list-full` with each directory stripped, line for line and same count — the install path is the frame, the applet name is its leaf (payload). (The author's --list / --list-full pair.)
statements: the two listings have the same number of lines
stripping the directory from each path yields the names, line for line

title: the self-append loop has no fixed point
claim: iterating F <- A+F+B (A,B nonempty) increases |F| by the same positive constant each step, so it never reaches a fixed point — the loop halts only by an external limit, never by itself. (The 121 MB file, deterministically, via a snapshot so no byte is read while it is written.)
statements: each step grows by the same positive constant inc = |A|+|B| (no fixed point)
strictly increasing — the sequence never settles

title: rev is its own inverse
claim: busybox rev reverses the bytes of a line, and rev applied twice is the identity (the direction switch).
statements: rev reverses a line (abc -> cba)
rev applied twice is the identity, for several byte strings

title: rot13 (tr) is its own inverse
claim: busybox tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' maps letters by rot13, leaves non-letters alone, and twice is the identity (the encoding switch).
statements: rot13 of Hello is Uryyb
rot13 leaves digits and punctuation unchanged (a1!z -> n1!m)
rot13 applied twice is the identity

title: XOR byte-distance is a metric — the tetrahedron's six edges
claim: over four equal-length vertices (WORD GOD OF of), each of the six unordered pairs has an XOR mask whose popcount is a Hamming distance, and that distance obeys the three metric laws: d(A,A)=0 (identity — distance 0 is only a copy, the mirror), d(A,B)=d(B,A) (symmetry), d(A,C)<=d(A,B)+d(B,C) (triangle). The count of six edges is a consequence of four vertices, not evidence of anything. (The author's tetra-mask, as a check that can say no.)
statements: identity — a vertex against itself is distance 0 (a copy, the mirror)
symmetry — d(A,B) = d(B,A) over all six unordered pairs
triangle inequality — d(A,C) <= d(A,B) + d(B,C) for all triples

title: redirection truncates the file before the command runs
claim: `> F` opens and empties F before the command runs, and `>` replaces F's content wholesale. (The command must not also read F — see ../pending for why `cat A F B > F` loops instead.)
statements: `:` produces no output, so `: > F` leaves F empty — truncation happens before the command
`>` replaces the content wholesale
